title: From man’s side: active faith and worthy repentance-works; what then is God’s remitting action?
source_text: XI. Porro ex iis quae dicta sunt patet, ut homo peccatorum remissionem consequatur, ex ejus parte nil amplius requiri, quam ut actuosa & efficaci fide ad Dei gratiam per Christum confugiat, & studeat operibus poenitentia dignis. Sed quaeritur quae sit illa Dei actio, per quam homo a reatu peccatorum absolvitur, & fit remissionis peccatorum particeps. Istud autem non videtur melius intelligi posse, quam si consideremus quomodo contrahatur reatus ille quem tollit remissio peccatorum, & cui opponitur quasi a diametro.
pass_a_gloss: Further, from what has been said it is clear that, for a man to obtain remission of sins, nothing more is required on his part than that with active and efficacious faith he flee to God’s grace through Christ, and study works worthy of repentance. But the question is asked what that action of God is through which a man is absolved from the guilt of sins and becomes a partaker of the remission of sins. But that does not seem able to be better understood than if we consider how that guilt is contracted which remission of sins removes, and to which it is opposed as if by a diameter.
pass_b_english: Man’s side: active efficacious faith fleeing to grace in Christ, plus repentance-worthy works.
God’s remitting act is best read by asking how the opposed guilt-relation is contracted.

choices.english: as if by a diameter / diametrically
choices.why: Remission opposed to guilt as contrary.
